Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-5821", "title": "Vasectomy", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "A vasectomy is a type of minor surgery that prevents a man from being able to get a woman pregnant."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It is a permanent form of birth control ."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "A vasectomy works by cutting the vas deferens, which are the tubes that carry the sperm out of the testicles."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Then the sperm can no longer reach the semen."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Semen is the fluid that the penis ejaculates (releases during orgasm)."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Since there are no sperm, the man cannot get a woman pregnant."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "The surgery is quick; it usually takes less than 30 minutes."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "You will probably be able to go home the same day."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "You may have some discomfort, bruising, and swelling for a few days."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "In most cases, you will fully recover in less than a week."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "A vasectomy is one of the most effective forms of birth control."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "But it takes about three months (or about 20 ejaculations) before it is effective."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "You will still need to use other birth control until you know that your semen doesn't have any more sperm in it."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "After two to three months, your health care provider will test your semen to make sure that there are no sperm in it."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Having a vasectomy does not affect your sex life."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "And it will not affect your ability to get an erection or have an orgasm."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Vasectomies can sometimes be reversed, but not always."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "It is done with a procedure to reconnect the vas deferens."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Another option if you decide to have children later might be to have sperm taken from your testicles."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "The sperm could then be used for in vitro fertilization (IVF)."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "It's also important to know that both a vasectomy reversal and IVF are expensive."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Having a vasectomy does not protect you from sexually transmitted infections (STIs), such as HIV ."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Using a condom every time you have anal, vaginal, or oral sex is the only way to protect against STIs."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Child Health and Human Development"}]}, {"id": "MLP-5825", "title": "Head Injuries", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Chances are you've bumped your head before."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Often, the injury is minor because your skull is hard and it protects your brain."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "But other head injuries can be more severe, such as a skull fracture, concussion , or traumatic brain injury ."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "A closed injury does not break through the skull."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "With an open, or penetrating, injury, an object pierces the skull and enters the brain."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Closed injuries are not always less severe than open injuries."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Some common causes of head injuries are falls , motor vehicle accidents , violence, and sports injuries ."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "It is important to know the warning signs of a moderate or severe head injury."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Get help immediately if the injured person has: A headache that gets worse or does not go away Repeated vomiting or nausea Convulsions or seizures An inability to wake up Dilated (enlarged) pupil in one or both eyes Slurred speech Weakness or numbness in the arms or legs Loss of coordination Increased confusion, restlessness, or agitation Doctors use a neurologic exam and imaging tests to make a diagnosis."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Treatment depends on the type of injury and how severe it is."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke"}]}, {"id": "MLP-1526", "title": "Legionnaires' Disease", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Legionnaires' disease is a serious type of pneumonia caused by Legionella bacteria ."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "The disease got its name when a group of people at an American Legion convention became ill with this type of pneumonia."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Legionella is found naturally in freshwater, such as lakes and rivers."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "But people usually only get sick from it when if it grows and spreads in man-made water systems."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "These systems can include hot tubs, fountains, and the plumbing systems of large buildings, such as hotels or nursing homes."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Legionella can also cause Pontiac fever."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "This is a milder, flu-like illness that doesn't infect your lungs."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "You can get the infection by breathing in mist or small drops of water that contain the bacteria."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "The mist may come from hot tubs, showers, or large building air conditioning units."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "You usually can't get infected by drinking water that contains the bacteria unless you aspirate it (accidentally breathe the water into your lungs)."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "The bacteria don't spread from person to person."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Disease outbreaks happen when many people are exposed to the same water source that contains the bacteria."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Who is more likely to develop Legionnaires' disease?"}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Most healthy people who come in contact with the bacteria do not become sick."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "You are more likely to develop an infection if you: Are over the age of 50 Are a current or former smoker Have a chronic (long-lasting) disease such as diabetes or kidney failure Have a chronic lung disease such as COPD or emphysema Have a weakened immune system due to a disease such as HIV or cancer or are taking medicines that suppress your immune system Live in a long-term care facility Have recently stayed in a hospital or had surgery requiring anesthesia What are the symptoms of Legionnaires' disease?"}, {"id": "S015", "text": "The symptoms usually show up 2 to 14 days after you were exposed to Legionella bacteria."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Most of the symptoms are similar to those of other types of pneumonia."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "But Legionnaires' disease may also cause gastrointestinal symptoms and mental changes."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "The symptoms of Legionnaires' disease may include: Cough High fever Chills Headache Chest pain Shortness of breath Fatigue Nausea and vomiting Diarrhea Confusion What other problems can Legionnaires' disease cause?"}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Legionnaires' disease can cause life-threatening complications such as respiratory failure , kidney failure, and sepsis ."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "About 1 out of every 10 people who get sick with Legionnaires' disease will die from complications of the illness."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "To find out if you have Legionnaires' disease, your health care provider will probably order a chest x-ray to see if you have pneumonia."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "If you do have it, lab tests such as a urine or sputum test can check for the Legionella bacteria."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Your provider may also order a blood test to see if you have been exposed to the bacteria."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "What are the treatments for Legionnaires' disease?"}, {"id": "S025", "text": "If you have Legionnaires' disease, you will likely need care in a hospital."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "Most people will recover, especially if they were healthy when they got the disease."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "Getting treatment early can increase the chances of getting better."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "You can lower your risk of getting Legionnaires' disease if you: Clean all your water-related devices regularly."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "This could include portable humidifiers, water heaters, air conditioners, and nasal rinses."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "If you haven't used your faucets and showerheads for a week or more, flush them by letting the hot and cold faucets run for at least two minutes before use."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "Avoid exposure to water sources such as decorative foundations or hot tubs if you don't know how well they are maintained."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "Use windshield cleaner in your wiper fluid tank in your car instead of water."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "Ask about how well your buildings' water systems are maintained."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention"}]}, {"id": "MLP-3754", "title": "Cardiomyopathy", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Cardiomyopathy is the name for diseases of the heart muscle."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "These diseases enlarge your heart muscle or make it thicker and more rigid than normal."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "In rare cases, scar tissue replaces the muscle tissue."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Some people live long, healthy lives with cardiomyopathy."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Some people don't even realize they have it."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "In others, however, it can make the heart less able to pump blood through the body."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "This can cause serious complications, including: Heart failure Abnormal heart rhythms Heart valve problems Sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) Heart attacks , high blood pressure , infections, and other diseases can all cause cardiomyopathy."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Some types of cardiomyopathy run in families."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "In many people, however, the cause is unknown."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Treatment might involve medicines, surgery, other medical procedures, and lifestyle changes."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "NIH: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute"}]}, {"id": "MLP-40", "title": "Skin Conditions", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "It covers the entire outside of your body."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "There are many ways that your skin protects your body and helps keep you healthy."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "For example, it: Holds body fluids in, which helps prevent you from getting dehydrated Keeps out harmful germs, which helps prevent infections Helps you feel things like heat, cold, and pain Helps control your body temperature Makes vitamin D when the sun shines on it Shields your body against heat and light What problems and conditions can affect your skin?"}, {"id": "S003", "text": "There are many different problems and conditions which can affect your skin."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Some of them can cause uncomfortable symptoms, such as itching , burning, redness, and rashes ."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Some of the more common skin conditions include: Acne , which causes pimples when hair follicles under your skin get clogged up Burns Cuts and scrapes Dandruff , flaking of the skin on your scalp (the top of your head) Eczema (atopic dermatitis), which causes inflammation, redness, and irritation of the skin Hives , which are red and sometimes itchy bumps on your skin Insect bites Psoriasis , which causes itchy, scaly red patches Skin cancer Skin infections How can I keep my skin healthy?"}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Since your skin protects your body in many ways, it's important to try to keep your skin healthy."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "For example, you can: Wear the right protective equipment, like gloves, long sleeves, knee and elbow pads, or helmets to protect against cuts, bumps and scrapes."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "If you do get a cut or scrape, clean it right away with soap and warm water."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Put on a bandage to protect it while it heals."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "When you are spending time outdoors, wear long sleeves and pants and use insect repellant to prevent insect bites."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Prevent sunburn by covering up and using sunscreen when outdoors."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Wash your hands often with soap and water."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "When you take a shower or bath, use warm (not hot) water."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Use mild cleansers and wash gently (don't scrub)."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Use moisturizers, like lotions, creams, or ointments, to prevent dry skin."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases"}]}]
